quote: Hi. This is Matt with I'm
stewart_read: The intro is garbled/cut off — the company name and reason for calling never land clearly before the customer starts asking who's calling. This is a legitimacy gap independent of the customer's own skepticism.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a transcription artifact (ASR dropout) rather than the rep actually failing to state the company name aloud.
coaching_implication: Have the rep confirm on a live call review whether the full company name and reason-for-call are being stated clearly in the first 10 seconds; this is the customer's first scam-check moment per intros.tesla/intros.standard.

quote: Oh, okay. So you're wanting, like, a ground mount system?
stewart_read: Rep misreads the customer's fear (a roof-mounted panel fire) as a request for ground-mount, showing a knowledge gap on panel types that briefly derails the conversation before the customer corrects him.
coaching_implication: Coach active listening on customer-described incidents before jumping to a technical label — let the customer finish the story first.

quote: So we we'll be liable for that, I I believe. We're
stewart_read: Rep guesses at liability rather than deferring immediately, then self-corrects by admitting he hasn't been trained on it yet. This is an honest-recovery pattern, not fabrication, but the initial guess was risky on a safety question.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should never guess on liability. Strategic read doesn't apply here — there's no deferred payoff to guessing wrong on a safety question.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the universal escape hatch language (setter_scope_discipline) so the rep defers to the specialist immediately on liability/safety questions instead of guessing first and correcting second.

quote: That would be so that would be a good question for the specialist.
stewart_read: By the third safety-related question (hazardous material disposal), the rep has settled into a clean, immediate defer-to-specialist pattern without guessing — the correct recovery from the earlier liability stumble.
coaching_implication: Point to this as the model response the rep should lead with from the first safety question, not just the third.

quote: Hell, no. I wish I could get that low. I wouldn't be working on a damn solar power.
stewart_read: Customer reacts with real emotional charge to a wrong low bill estimate, revealing genuine bill pain and volunteering his real number moments later. This is a strong anchor the rep captured but never flipped into 'that's exactly what this program targets.'
coaching_implication: Coach the flip: acknowledge the number, then explicitly tie the appointment to solving that specific pain rather than moving straight to the next verify item.

quote: Y'all wanna take up a collection with a company on my light bill and help me out or something?
stewart_read: This reads as a fixed-income/financial-hardship disclosure dressed as a joke — the customer is signaling real strain with his bill. The rep's response ('I'm not sure, honestly... I don't know all that') treats it as an unanswerable logistics question rather than a vulnerability moment worth a human acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep missed a trust-gift moment. Strategic read doesn't hold — there's no visible later payoff from deferring empathy here.
coaching_implication: Coach a brief human acknowledgment ('sounds like that bill's been rough on you') before redirecting to the specialist, rather than only redirecting.
